title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_0LD0LF_0LB0LE_1LA1LD_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_0LD0LF_0LB0LE_1LA1LD_---0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A left bouncer over a 10 background carries a solid block of 1s that grows, splits and re-forms at irregular times (the staircase in the space-time diagram); the slow right end is a periodic 1111 0 1 0 1 0 pattern; open.

Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone), 10 shift rules of the sweeps; the rest of the description below is observation of the run, marked as such.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 40,882 cells have been visited and 26,599 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.453). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.131).

claims.title: 10 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: B and A turn 10/01 into 11 rightward (filling a block), C, D and E erase leftward (0101 → 0100, 1010 → 0010 …). Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (F reading 0) needs 00010 to the right of the head; any left side. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer with a wandering solid block
claims.text: The tape has three parts. Far left: the 10 background of a bouncer that grows to the left like the square root of the step count. Far right (the slow side, 120 cells after 109 steps): a periodic pattern (1111 0 1 0 1 0) repeated, which only grows by a cell now and then. In between: one or two solid blocks of 1s, thousands of cells long, separated by stretches of 10.

claims.text: Not known. F reading 0 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows this only with 00010 to the right of the head.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 40,882 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

facts.value: bouncer with a wandering solid block

sections.heading: What the machine does: bouncer with a wandering solid block
html: The tape has three parts. Far left: the 10 background of a bouncer that grows to the left like the square root of the step count. Far right (the slow side, 115 cells right of the start after 109 steps): a periodic pattern (1111 0 1 0 1 0) repeated, which only grows by a cell now and then. In between: one or two solid blocks of 1s, thousands of cells long, separated by stretches of 10.

Rightward sweeps fill 10 into 11 (rules sweep_rB_10, sweep_rA_01), leftward sweeps cut solid stretches back into 10 or 0010. So the solid block is moved, grown and cut: e.g. at step 4·107 the tape reads 1^3 0 (10)* 1 0 1^964 0 (10)* 1 0 1 0 1^1388 E> (10)* …, at 3·108 1^7533 B> (10)* … (a single block), at 5.4·108 1^6847 0 (10)* 1 0 1^925 A>0 (10)* ….

Each time a block runs into the right part, the right end gets a few new cells, which is why the slow side grows in rare steps (right extent ~ t0.13). The lengths of the blocks look irregular; we have no rule for them.

sections.heading: What a halt would require
html: F reading 0 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows this only with 00010 to the right of the head.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html:
• Sweeps (lean/Sweeps.lean, kernel): B and A turn 10/01 into 11 rightward (filling a block), C, D and E erase leftward (0101 → 0100, 1010 → 0010 …); for every number of copies and every tape around.
  • Bounded run (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in 107 steps (native), 10,000 (kernel); the halting transition is the only way to stop.
Everything else on this page is observation of the simulated run (heuristic). Nothing here decides halting.

sections.heading: What would move it forward
html: Sample the run each time a solid block is born or dies, record the block lengths, and look for a map between them (the staircase suggests a Collatz-like map on the block length).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.453). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.131).
After 109 steps the tape spans 40,882 cells (30,269 left of the start, 115 right), with a density of 1s of 0.651.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
